questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to choose the perfect gift for your mother
How kindness helps the giver and even politics
Why people became less kind during the pandemic
How businesses can make more money by being fair
questions.why: They discuss the science showing kindness makes us feel good, and a movement for compassion in politics.

questions.q: How did Sam feel after giving her mum flowers?
options: Worried that her mum didn't like them
Sorry that she had spent so much money
Surprised that her mum was so upset
Good, because she'd made her mum happy
questions.why: Sam says, 'It felt good knowing I'd made her happy.'

questions.q: What are psychologists starting to prove, according to Neil?
options: Being kind feels as good as receiving kindness
Receiving kindness feels better than giving it
Most people are kind only to their families
Random acts of kindness are becoming rare
questions.why: He says we feel just as good being kind to someone else as when someone is kind to us.

questions.q: What shows that psychologists are very interested in kindness?
options: Many new university courses on kindness
A TV series about kind people
Over a thousand papers on it in ten years
A new law requiring kindness at work
questions.why: Neil says over a thousand academic papers including the term 'kindness' were written in the past decade.

questions.q: According to Dr Dan Campbell-Meiklejohn, what happens in our brain when we're kind?
options: It becomes tired and needs to rest
It reacts like it does to tasty food
It feels the same as when we lose money
It becomes less active than usual
questions.why: He says the parts active when we eat yummy food or have a nice surprise become active when we're kind.

questions.q: Why might being kind seem counter-intuitive to some people?
options: Because kind people are often not trusted
Because it takes a lot of time to be kind
Because other people rarely say thank you
Giving things away can feel like a loss
questions.why: Neil says for some people giving something away equals losing it, so being kind seems counter-intuitive.

questions.q: What does Neil wonder about business and politics?
options: Whether they are kinder than personal life
Whether politicians give enough money away
Whether kindness has any place in them
Whether women should lead more companies
questions.why: He asks about 'the ruthless world of business or politics – surely there's no place for kindness there?'

questions.q: What does Jennifer Nagel say about compassion in politics?
options: It makes fairer societies and takes courage
It is a nice idea but not really practical
It only works in very small countries
It makes politicians look weak to voters
questions.why: She says it leads to fairer societies and lower crime, and 'it actually takes courage to act with compassion'.
